issues.issue: Original printed Chapter XCVII maps to stable editorial XCVIII because an earlier numbered chapter numeral was duplicated.
The first-edition chapter spans original PDF516–520 (printed 482–486), and the distinct Book III title begins original PDF521.
The original eight-leaf planetary-hour numeric table PDF508–515 is preserved in B04t, but its approximately 1,488 numeric clock cells have not all been independently digitized.
Page-level scans and paraphrases are source witnesses, not a complete independent second diplomatic transcription.
Historical printed seven-planet weekday names use 1647 glyphs; rendered planet names should not be confused with modern planetary science.
The astrological ruler of a day or hour is a symbolic prescription, not an empirically established human influence.
The seven-planet hourly sequence continues over sunrise/sunset, so an hour number must not reset the planet cycle at midnight or sunset.
Day/night are separately divided by sunrise and sunset into twelve equal portions each; a constant sixty-minute clock hour violates source requirements outside equal-day idealization.
Lilly's ingress of Sun into Aries or Libra yields exact sixty-minute idealization; geographic latitude, atmospheric refraction and modern astronomical times remain independently unresolved.
Table page routing depends on left/right zodiac sun-sign margin and daylight-versus-night; not all historical cross-margin numbers have been recalculated.
The example date appears 15 March 1646/7, with Old Style/New Style year interpretation unresolved; do not silently convert to modern date.
The Sun at about 4°47 Aries is an author-provided zodiac longitude not independently checked against modern historical ephemeris.
Example row selection 3° or 6° Aries is approximate and uses three-degree table spacing; exact interpolation rule is not specified.
The example 5:47 AM sunrise and 6:13 PM sunset are table values, not independently authenticated historical observed clock times.
The clock boundaries have minute rounding; calculated hour length 64 minutes is based on the printed table, not complete astronomical parity.
The 9:30AM, 5:20PM and 11:10PM outputs are deterministic arithmetic from printed values and Chaldean sequence only, not observed cases or prospective astrology tests.
At an exact boundary, inclusivity/tie-breaking is not defined by these examples; tests avoid this ambiguity.
Day length 64m and night length 56m are idealized complementary durations for an example and may vary by date/place.
The mirrored sign claim concerning Taurus/Leo and Virgo/Aries must not be generalized beyond the source table symmetry without independent numerical verification.
After-noon 5:20PM and late-night 11:10PM worked examples refer to the same example Monday; no independent people or events are present.
The 11:10PM example source time is written in period style as eleven hours ten minutes after noon; normalized civil time is an interpretation.
The table's noon/midnight divisions may use contemporary clock/time conventions; no universal time zone is inferred.
Lilly's prescriptions for giving physic, collecting herbs, making sigils/images/lamens lack demonstrated medical, botanical or occult efficacy.
No current person should change medical care on the basis of historical planetary-hour selection.
His statement that no worthy work can proceed without planetary hours is authorial confidence, not an empirical controlled finding.
The authorial conclusion invokes divine assistance, an Anima Mundi and a moral defense; these are historical intellectual and religious context, not chart rules.
Lilly's assertions about receiving no help or critics' eventual responses are autobiographical claims without independent outside records.
The date 11 June 1647 appears in the signed conclusion, distinct from the 1646/7 worked example date and the Book III title.

The Book III title promises Trutine of Hermes, Animodar, life-accident birth-time rectification, Directions/Revolutions/Profections/Transits; those methods are not extracted or independently validated here.
Finishing these printed-prose page records does not complete Book II numeric transcription; no independent empirical predictions or runtime model promotions have occurred.
